claims.text: The baseline AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy has a uniform, fine lamellar structure.
The baseline alloy has inadequate resistance to long-term creep.
The baseline alloy has inadequate corrosion resistance under extreme temperature fluctuations.
Annealing at approximately 900°C in a low-oxygen atmosphere for several hours, followed by controlled cooling, will induce nanoscale oxide particles in the alloy.
The induced nanoscale oxide particles will be uniformly dispersed along the lamellar interfaces.
The induced oxide particles may consist of Al2O3.
Nanoscale oxide particles at lamellar interfaces will act as pinning centers.
The nanoscale oxide particles will hinder dislocation glide.
The nanoscale oxide particles will hinder grain-boundary sliding.
The nanoscale oxide particles will act as local diffusion barriers to corrosive species.
Impeded dislocation glide and grain-boundary sliding will stabilize the microstructure against creep deformation.
The proposed treatment will markedly reduce room-temperature creep relative to the unmodified alloy.
The proposed treatment will improve corrosion stability during extreme temperature fluctuations relative to the unmodified alloy.
The proposed treatment will retain a satisfactory strength–ductility balance.
The unmodified cast and thermomechanically processed baseline lacks a nano-oxide dispersion.
The expected improvements require precise control of annealing temperature, oxygen level, and cooling rate.
Departures from the specified processing window may cause uneven precipitate distributions.
Departures from the specified processing window may cause detrimental phase changes that limit effectiveness.
